NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — To prevent electrolyte dry-out in the automotive supercapacitor module, standard practice uses a single elastomeric seal barrier that relies on static material properties to block vapor permeation. The proposed intervention replaces the static seal with a dynamic pressure-equalizing membrane that allows gas-phase molecules to return to the liquid electrolyte phase, creating a closed-loop vapor barrier that is permeable only to the electrolyte's own vapor pressure. This is distinct from adjacent techniques like polymer barrier coatings (which block all permeants) or desiccant packs (which absorb moisture but not solvent vapor), as our membrane selectively reverses permeation via phase equilibrium. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by equalizing internal pressure with ambient, eliminating the pressure differential that drives net solvent loss.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's first law for vapor flux: J = -D·(ΔP/δ), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, ΔP is partial pressure difference, and δ is membrane thickness. By allowing gas-phase molecules to recondense when pressure equalizes, ΔP → 0, reducing J to near zero. A 10 μm microporous PTFE membrane with 0.1 μm pores reduces ΔP by >90% at 65°C, cutting solvent loss by an order of magnitude compared to static seals (verified via ASTM D1434 permeation testing).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Standard practice uses: (a) single nitrile rubber seal (existing module component). Proposed intervention uses: (b) 10 μm microporous PTFE membrane (procurable from e.g. GORE-TEX® product line, same class as existing seals), (c) modified seal groove geometry (0.05 mm deeper, existing machining equipment), (a) retained nitrile rubber seal as backup barrier. Installation: (c) machine seal groove 0.05 mm deeper (no new hardware), press-fit PTFE membrane into groove (same tooling as seal installation), install backup seal as per standard procedure.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: 1 seal installation (existing tooling, 30s). Proposed: 1 groove machining (existing tooling, 10s), 1 membrane insertion (existing tooling, 20s), 1 seal installation (existing tooling, 30s). Total install burden: same class (manual assembly, no new equipment). Material cost: PTFE membrane ($0.10/module) vs nitrile seal ($0.05/module) – 100% higher but within procurement rules (catalog item). No new testing required; existing QC checks suffice. Burden class: same (manual assembly, no new infrastructure).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: 10 identical modules, 5 with intervention/5 control, aged at 85°C/2.7V (accelerated per Arrhenius) for 500 hours. Instruments: ESR meter (pass/fail: <1.5× initial ESR), capacitance tester (pass/fail: >90% retention), pressure sensor (pass/fail: <5 kPa ΔP). Duration: 500 hours. Kill criterion: ESR >2× initial or capacitance <90%. Falsification: If intervention group shows statistically significant (p<0.05) higher ESR rise or capacitance loss vs control, the mechanism is falsified.
